_readme.what: Composition path tree for dub / electro-dub (the second genre tree; see psydub.json for the format contract and ledger.json for cross-song memory).
_readme.genre_basis: Research 2026-09-22 (MusicRadar/reggae programming guides + Roland RE-201 documentation): one-drop puts kick+rim on BEAT 3 with beat 1 left open; steppers puts the kick on all four quarters; the skank is a short clipped chord on the OFFBEATS (the '&' of each beat); dub space comes from a TAPE ECHO with the filter INSIDE the feedback loop, wow 5-12% / flutter 3-8%, and a feedback arc (normal 35% -> throw 60% -> regen 80% -> exit 20%); spring reverb is subtle (wet 8-20%), not a large wash.
_readme.measured_on: dub_embers, 2026-09-22 (96 BPM, C minor, 120 bars, 15 tracks) — every recipe below carries the values actually used.

phases.rule: timeline-shape writers -> timeline-dependent writers -> readers. Measurement (mix) is LAST and nothing writes after it.
phases.why: Anything that references a SECTION, a bar boundary or the total length is a function of the finished timeline and must be written after `arrangement` - written earlier it resolves against a provisional timeline and is silently wrong (the mutation-order trap). This tree has no `space` node (its gestures live in `movement`), so nothing needed moving on 2026-09-23.
phases.rides: The timeline-final recipes (whole-track arcs, send/bus return rides, per-section staging) live in the psydub tree's `rides` node and apply here unchanged - see docs/paths/psydub.json.
phases.rerun: The pass must be re-runnable: address automation lanes BY PARAMID, pass `clear: true` to automation_preset, and use add_automation_lane {replace:true} to take ownership of a lane whose name changed between runs.

_readme.how: same contract as psydub.json: walk the nodes in order, one option each, filter by forbids + the ledger, record the path in the brief, run each option's gate.

foundation.question: Tempo / key / mode — and whether the key can be matched to the source material.

options.name: C minor at 96 BPM — chosen to match the MIDI corpus labels
options.why: E:\midi riff packs are labelled and, when analysed, are overwhelmingly C Natural Minor. Setting the project to C minor (root 0, scaleMode 1) makes the modal snippets agree BY CONSTRUCTION instead of by transposition, which removes the whole class of sour-note errors.

options.name: Steppers at 100-105 BPM
options.why: Research range for steppers; more forward drive than one-drop.

percussion_pool.question: 4-8 mostly non-overlapping percussive layers, randomly picked from the corpus.

options.name: 7 layers, seeded random one-shots, loop-rejected
options.why: Measured recipe that worked: kick / rim / closed hat / open hat / shaker / conga / tom, each a seeded random pick across the registered drum kits, FILTERED to one-shots (duration <= 3 s, no 'loop'/'break'/'bpm' markers). Blind randomness picked a 105 BPM hat LOOP, a 162 BPM shaker break and a kick+snare+tom loop — all of which would have broken the non-overlap and imported a stray tempo.

recipe.search: search_library per role across the kits, seeded shuffle, take the first

gate.audit: no two layers share a role or a loop tempo; every sample durationSeconds <= 3.0

options.name: 4 layers (kick, rim, hat, perc)
options.why: Minimum that still reads as a riddim; use when the mix is already dense.

groove.question: The beat. THIS is where dub's identity lives, and where the psytrance gates fight you.

options.name: Steppers kick + rim on beat 3, clap on 2-and-4
options.why: Measured: kick on all 4 quarters (steppers), rim on beat 3 (the one-drop accent), plus a clap on 2-and-4. The clap is an electro-reggae hybrid that ALSO satisfies `audit_song_structure`'s backbeat gate — a pure one-drop fails that gate by design.

recipe.kick: 4 per bar + an extra kick at 2.75 on the last bar of every 8
recipe.clap: beats 1 and 3 (0-indexed) + a 3.75 grace hit every 8 bars
recipe.hats: closed offbeat 8ths (0.5/1.5/2.5/3.5), open hat at 3.5 every 4 bars

options.name: Pure one-drop (no kick on beat 1, rim on 3)
options.why: The authentic roots groove: beat 1 stays open. Expect `allDropsHaveBackbeat` to FAIL under the default — record it in the brief rather than distorting the groove, or audit with `expectBackbeat:false` (2026-09-23) to skip the psytrance-shaped gate.

gate.acknowledge: structure backbeat gate will fail by design

chords.question: The harmonic bed — jazzy 7ths/9ths, mellow but dissonant, modulated per note.

options.name: Cm9 / Fm9 vamp split across 3 independently-modulated voices
options.why: Measured: Cm9 (C Eb G Bb D) alternating with Fm9 (F Ab C Eb G) over 4-bar blocks, split as low = C2+G2, mid = Eb3+Bb3, high = D4. The 9th (D) sits a semitone above the minor 3rd (Eb) — that half-step IS the 'mellow but dissonant' cluster. Each voice carries its OWN slow LFO (0.07 / 0.11 / 0.17 Hz) into the synth Cutoff, so the chord beats against itself and thickens. `tone_verity` confirmed the fundamentals land on G, Bb and D (fifth, 7th, 9th).

recipe.tracks: 3 x sub_synth (Virus sysex), Cutoff ~1800 (the closed-filter trap applies)
recipe.notes: one sustained note per chord tone per 8-bar block (30-beat duration)
recipe.modulation: add_lfo + set_lfo_param per voice, targetParamID 107 (synth Cutoff), rateSync 0, distinct rates

gate.tone_verity: f0 is a chord tone for every pad voice

options.name: One chord track via generate_chord
options.why: Cheaper (one track, chordType Minor 9 / Dominant 9, voicing + inversion available), but per-note modulation is impossible on a single track — you get one LFO for the whole chord.

skank.question: The dub chord chop and its echo — the genre's signature gesture.

options.name: 3/16 Rhodes ostinato through a tape-echo chain
options.why: Measured: a DX7 'RHODES EGH' voice (fm_synth, `D:\pdf\Dexed Presets\1980 Sounds\Keys.syx` voiceIndex 3) chopping the chord every 3/16 (0.75 beats, dotted-8th hemiola) across the chord tones, through saturator -> delay (sync, Division 4 = dotted-1/8 = 3/16, feedback 0.62, mix 0.34) -> LPF 3.2 kHz -> small reverb (room 0.30, wet 0.18). A 0.6 Hz LFO on the delay TIME supplies tape wow; an `adsr` envelope on the delay Feedback gives the research's feedback arc 0.35 -> 0.80; a 0.09 Hz LFO on Pan drifts the repeats.

recipe.voice: fm_synth_import_sysex Keys.syx voiceIndex 3 (iterate voiceIndex and read voiceName to find an EP)
recipe.placement: 5 hits per bar at 0.75-beat spacing + a 3.75 wrap hit, 4 chord tones per hit, duration 0.22
recipe.echo: saturator 8 dB drive -> delay -> LPF 3200 Hz AFTER the delay (HDAW has no in-loop filter; an output filter darkens the repeats but does NOT progressively darken each generation)
recipe.modulation: LFO 0.6 Hz depth 0.06 -> delay Time (paramID 300); LFO 0.09 Hz -> Pan (2)

gate.mix_diff: the chop measurably changes rms/high band vs the same render without it

options.known_limit: no in-loop filtering and no true send bus: the repeats darken once, not per generation, and the echo sits on the track rather than on a shared return

options.name: Classic one-drop skank on the offbeat 8ths
options.why: The research standard: short clipped chord on the '&' of every beat (steps 3/7/11/15), 1/16-1/8 long, high-passed so it does not fight the bass. Less busy than the 3/16 ostinato.

modal.question: Mid-range melodic material over the bed — sourced, key-verified, and filter-shaped.

options.name: Corpus riff gated by analyze_midi_file, on 2 mono instruments
options.why: Measured: of 104 files labelled '[C] [Natural Minor]', only 55 analysed as C + Natural Minor — 8 had a different root and TWO analysed as Major despite the label. Gate on `fingerprint.rootNote % 12 == 0 AND fingerprint.scaleType == 1`, then place `patterns[].notes` (per-bar {pitch, startBeat, durationBeats, velocity}) with add_notes, repeated across sections.

recipe.select: analyze_midi_file, keep only C + Natural Minor
recipe.place: the 8-bar riff repeated per section on two instruments (one at pitch, one an octave down)
recipe.shape: generate_automation_envelope on the filter Cutoff (paramID 200): 'saw' 16 cycles / 'adsr' 24 cycles across the arrangement

gate.analyze_midi_file: root%12==0 and scaleType==1 for every snippet used

options.name: Generate the modal line instead of sourcing it
options.why: generate_phrase with a scale-aware style keeps the mode by construction and avoids corpus hunting, at the cost of the human phrasing a real riff has.

arrangement.question: Where the kick is absent and where the drums drop out entirely.

options.name: Intro with no kick + a full drum drop-out in the breakdown
options.why: Measured: intro = rim + shaker only (no kick — the one-drop 'hole'), the breakdown drops ALL drums leaving bass + echo (the classic dub move), drops = full hybrid groove. Produced an 8 dB arc over a 300 s track.

recipe.sections: intro 8 / build1 16 / drop1 32 / break 16 / build2 16 / drop2 32 (120 bars at 96 BPM = 5:00)

options.name: Continuous groove (no drum drop-out)
options.why: Simpler and safer for a DJ-friendly edit; loses the signature dub gesture.

movement.question: Coverage + musical movement (reuse the psydub node's options).

options.name: One targeted LFO per sounding track

recipe.note: add_lfo + set_lfo_param, targetParamID = the first automatable param of the slot that matters

options.name: Rely on gesture lanes (>= 3 points counts)
Render once at a safe master, read the peak, rescale
options.why: Measured: rendering at master 0.5 gave peak 0.954 with rms 0.177 — inside the 0.85-0.95 window, so NO second render was needed. Watch the bass band: this arrangement measured bass:high = 38:1, so trim the bass fader (0.72) before blaming the master.

options.name: Window probe instead of a full canary (cheapest rescale)
options.why: Measured 2026-09-22 (dub_embers, 300 s render that takes ~7 min): `verify_part {trackIndex, startBeat, endBeat, windowSeconds}` on a SHORT window inside the LOUDEST section returns `mixPeak` in seconds. Set a safe master (0.30), probe the loudest drop, then master = 0.90 / (mixPeak / 0.30). On dub_embers the probe read mixPeak 0.675 at 0.30 -> true peak 2.25 -> master 0.395, in ~2 s instead of a 7-minute canary render.
options.caveat: the window must contain the global peak — pick the loudest drop, and expect the reading to be a hair optimistic if the true peak is a single transient elsewhere

options.name: Canary at 0.25 then exact master
options.why: Braver but costs an extra render; use when the mix is expected to clip.

traps.compressor-eats-the-bass: A default `compressor` slot (Threshold -20 dB, Ratio 4:1) on the bass made the bassline inaudible: soloPeak measured 0.032 while a pad voice at the SAME pitches measured 0.116. Raising Threshold to -6 dB and Ratio to 2:1 doubled the bass (0.032 -> 0.060) and the rewritten riff plus fader 1.0 took it to 0.105. The synth was hot and the compressor was clamping it. ALWAYS audition a bass solo with `verify_part` inside a DROP window before mixing around it — and note that an audition from beat 0 measures SILENCE if the track (like a dub bass) has no clip in the intro.
traps.static-bassline: Root-third-fifth on every bar is not a bassline. User feedback on dub_embers: 'I don't really hear a distinct bassline'. Fix: a 4-bar riff shape with a hook bar (octave jump + syncopation) and rests, i-i-iv-i, answering the offbeat skank by playing ON the beats.
traps.claps-are-an-instrument: Don't reserve claps for a backbeat-fix. User feedback: 'claps exist, you can use them! you can put delay on them too, with feedback.' Give the clap its own delay (dotted-1/8, feedback ~0.58, mix ~0.40) plus pickup hits every 2 bars and offbeat doubles every 8.
traps.chop-clarity: A 3/16 chop can be present and still unhearable: `verify_part` showed the Rhodes skank at soloPeak 0.34 (loud) while it read as a wash in the mix. The fixes were subtractive and additive at once — delay Mix 0.34 -> 0.18 (less smearing), LPF 3.2k -> 8k (let it speak), +3 dB presence EQ at 3 kHz, and a -2.5 dB dip at 2.5 kHz on the KICK to unmask it.
traps.pad-modulation-must-be-long: User feedback: the background chord 'could use more / longer+subtle modulation'. Fast shallow LFOs (0.07-0.17 Hz, depth 0.45) read as static. Fix: depth down to ~0.22 AND a SECOND LFO per voice at 0.017-0.031 Hz (30-60 s cycles) on a different target, plus envelope cycles stretched from 8 to 3 over the arrangement (~100 s sweeps).
traps.slot-must-exist: `set_internal_fx_param` on a slot index that does not exist returns 'slot not found' and DOES NOTHING — and if you are not checking the error it looks like the write landed. Measured 2026-09-22: three +2 dB pad EQ writes went to slot 3 on tracks that only had chorus(1)+reverb(2); the fix was `add_fx {fxType:'eq'}` first. Always `list_fx_params {trackId, slotIndex}` before writing a param into a chain you did not build.
traps.tonal-balance-recipe: When the mix bands come out bass-dominant (measured 38,983 bass vs 1,330 high = 29:1), the fix is four moves at once, not a master change: (1) trim where kick and bass FIGHT — kick -4 dB @42 Hz (below its punch) plus fader 0.82, bass Sub Level 0.85 -> 0.60 and Cutoff 600 -> 450; (2) lift the highs at source — closed hat +3.5 dB @9 kHz, shaker +2.5 dB @7 kHz; (3) add body — +2 dB @500 Hz on the pad voices, skank LPF 3.2k -> 10k; (4) NARROW the modal filter envelopes (0.15-0.95 of the sweep range -> 0.55-0.85) so the riffs sit in a clear band instead of washing across it.
traps.label-trust: MIDI pack filenames lie. 104 files named '[C] [Natural Minor]' produced only 55 that analysed as C + Natural Minor; 2 analysed as MAJOR. Always gate on analyze_midi_file's fingerprint (rootNote % 12 == 0 and scaleType == 1).
traps.loop-vs-oneshot: Seeded random sample picks return LOOPS unless filtered. A 105 BPM hat loop, a 162 BPM shaker break and a kick+snare+tom loop were all picked before the duration/name filter went in — each would have imported a stray tempo or overlapped other layers.
traps.backbeat-gate-vs-dub: `audit_song_structure.allDropsHaveBackbeat` wants 2-and-4; a roots one-drop (rim on beat 3) fails it by design. Hybridise with a clap on 2-and-4, record the failure as intentional, or pass `expectBackbeat:false` to the audit (2026-09-23) to skip the gate. Never move the rim to 2-and-4.
traps.no-in-loop-filter: HDAW's delay has no filter inside the feedback loop (params: Time, Feedback, Mix, Sync, Division), so tape-echo repeats cannot be progressively darkened. Put a filter AFTER the delay and accept one-generation darkening; use lower feedback (<= 0.62) to stop low-end build-up instead.
traps.no-sends: RESOLVED 2026-09-22/23 - buses/sends ARE creatable and listable (add_bus / add_send / remove_bus / remove_send, list_buses) and send levels are AUTOMATABLE as of 2026-09-23 (paramID 2000 + sendIndex), so the research's send-based dub routing CAN be built on a shared bus return - not just per-track FX + gesture lanes. Original gap (docs/composition-toolkit.md, 'Known capability gap'): buses/sends had no agent surface.
traps.render-time: Render time scales with automation density: 300 s of a 14-track / ~6k-note / ~15k-automation-point arrangement took 410 s (slower than realtime), where a 9-track sampler-only render of the same length took ~10 s. Budget two renders (measure + final) as a quarter hour on a dense dub arrangement.
traps.sysex-cutoff: Same trap as psydub.json: after sub_synth_import_sysex the virus filter lands as-is, so a closed patch renders near-silent at Cutoff 20 Hz. Set it per role (bass ~260, pad ~1800) before auditioning.

measured_baseline.key_check: Cm9/Fm9 vamp in C minor; tone_verity f0 read G, Bb, D on the pad voices (fifth, 7th, 9th) and C on the skank — no sour tones
